headline: Medium risk: EMQX’s broad network egress can leak IoT data, while LlamaFactory’s no-network/no-filesystem profile limits direct interaction harms.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared communication channel is documented: EMQX has HTTP API and broad egress, while LlamaFactory has no clipboard, files, stdin/stdout, MCP, or browser surfaces. Without a bridge, prompt injection from one into the other is not plausible from the profiles alone.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator copies EMQX output into LlamaFactory prompts, injection becomes possible.
IF a shared filesystem or message queue is added between them, the pathway changes.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate hosts or containers.
Do not pipe EMQX output into LlamaFactory prompts without sanitization.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to any bridged messages.
requires-engineering: enforce allowlisted prompt templates for any orchestration layer.

B_data_leakage.rationale: EMQX touches IoT data and has broad network egress, so it can transmit sensitive operational data. LlamaFactory itself shows no direct egress or file access, so the pairwise leakage path is mainly through EMQX’s outbound traffic rather than a shared workspace. The interaction is indirect, but default egress makes leakage plausible.
conditions: IF EMQX is connected to production IoT telemetry, outbound leakage impact increases.
IF an operator routes EMQX logs or payloads into LlamaFactory externally, additional leakage paths appear.
mitigations: Restrict EMQX egress to approved endpoints.
Redact IoT payloads before any handoff to LlamaFactory.
Run both agents in separate network zones.
requires-engineering: add DLP controls on EMQX outbound traffic.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: The profiles do not show overlapping write surfaces: EMQX exposes HTTP API and network egress, while LlamaFactory has no filesystem write, shell, subprocess, or git modification capability. With no shared mutable resource documented, write conflict is not plausible from the pair.
conditions: IF both agents are later granted write access to the same directory, conflict risk appears.
IF a shared database or git repo is introduced, coordination becomes necessary.
mitigations: Keep mutable resources single-writer.
Separate deployment directories for each agent.
Avoid granting LlamaFactory write permissions.
requires-engineering: add locking around any shared state.

D_cascading_error.rationale: EMQX can emit IoT-related outputs, but LlamaFactory has no documented action-taking authority, shell, or network egress, so it is unlikely to execute downstream harmful actions. Any cascade would require an external orchestrator to treat EMQX output as authoritative and then act on it.
conditions: IF an orchestrator feeds EMQX outputs into LlamaFactory without verification, cascade risk increases.
IF LlamaFactory is wrapped by another agent that can send emails or modify systems, the blast radius expands.
mitigations: Insert a human review step before acting on EMQX outputs.
Require schema validation on any EMQX-to-LlamaFactory handoff.
Log source provenance for all forwarded facts.
requires-engineering: add automated consistency checks before downstream actions.

E_compliance.rationale: Only EMQX is clearly associated with IoT data, and no residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented for LlamaFactory. Because the pair lacks explicit compliance metadata, the main issue is limited to potential handling gaps rather than a proven breach pathway.
conditions: IF IoT data includes regulated personal data, compliance review is required.
IF either deployment stores data outside the operator’s approved region, residency concerns arise.
mitigations: Classify the IoT data before routing it.
Confirm retention settings for EMQX logs.
Avoid sending regulated data into LlamaFactory workflows.
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls for both systems.
